To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the salsa dance industry relies on racial scripts that construct difference in order to sell salsa as an exotic and cosmopolitan product.
the racialised scripts of cosmopolitan consumption are highly ambiguous and that they rely on racialised difference in order to sell salsa as a desirable commodity.

the cosmopolitan consumption of racialised difference in salsa dance in Europe relies on racial scripts and that only difference that can be incorporated through consumption is valued as ‘positive’ in the current political context.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how racialised difference is consumed in the salsa dance industry in Britain.
the ways in which the racialisation of salsa is used to construct a cosmopolitan subject.
how the racialisation of difference is central to cosmopolitan consumption and therefore to the cosmopolitan project.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cosmopolitanism is a discourse that is highly ambivalent and that can be used as a strategy of exclusion as well as inclusion.
cosmopolitanism is not the answer to multiculturalism.
the consumption of difference is a process that is racialised, and that the consumption of racialised difference is a process of cosmopolitanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
cosmopolitanism is an ambiguous concept, which can be used to describe the consumption of difference, but that the consumption of difference is not necessarily cosmopolitan.
cosmopolitanism is a form of consumption that relies on racialised processes of othering and exoticising to be possible in the first place.
we have shown that the salsa dance industry is not as open as it claims to be.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consumption of difference is not necessarily a positive process.
cosmopolitan consumption is a form of cultural appropriation that can only be sustained by racialised scripts that are not open to all.
cosmopolitanism is not a universal practice but rather a discourse that is mobilised by the industry to sell difference.
